Marcus does not want details of his recovery discussed with family, and nurse Jamison agreed to keep family updates within the logistics scope he set. The TEE-guided cardioversion wording is acceptable in Marcus's portal copy but must not be used in family or voicemail messages. Marcus also does not want another patient or another family member to hear his schedule or contact notes, and wants his chart kept separate from other patients' charts. Marcus appreciates that the same-surname caution remains in place because the names were getting mixed up earlier, and the caution should stay active. states.content: Cardioversion was the plan for Marcus Reed's atrial fibrillation rhythm control. Because the timing of his Monday-night apixaban dose was uncertain, Dr. Patel changed the approach from direct cardioversion to TEE-guided cardioversion so a clot could be checked for first while still avoiding an unnecessary delay. Dr. Patel proceeded with TEE-guided cardioversion today, pending TEE findings; the TEE was to confirm there is no clot before the shock. Dr. Patel confirmed that if the TEE was clear, the cardioversion would proceed immediately today. The TEE was completed and showed no left atrial appendage thrombus, so synchronized cardioversion was performed and sinus rhythm was restored. The Wednesday, March 11 slot was released, and the Thursday, March 12 slot was taken by an add-on case; the TEE-guided cardioversion was scheduled for Friday, March 13 at 12:30 PM with 11:00 AM arrival at the cardiac procedures unit on the third floor. Reception Ana reconfirmed the Friday arrival: March 13, 11:00 AM, cardiac procedures unit, third floor. Scheduler Terry updated the arrival letter in the portal, and Marcus's own portal copy prep line says TEE-guided cardioversion. Marcus requested that the procedure slot details be put in the chart. Dr. Patel reviewed the labs and stated they were acceptable for outpatient cardioversion, satisfying the pending-labs condition; full medication history reconciliation remains part of the plan. Dr. Patel instructed that Marcus must not miss any apixaban doses at all between now and cardioversion, and to continue apixaban exactly as prescribed without missing any further doses. Pharmacist Klein confirmed apixaban stays at 5 mg twice daily and Marcus must not stop or skip it on his own unless the cardiologist specifically says otherwise. The only routine periprocedural hold discussed was lisinopril on the morning of the procedure once the date was confirmed. Nurse Jamison will bring Marcus back first for his cardiology rhythm clinic visit. Dr. Patel confirmed the follow-up plan: Monday, March 16 nurse callback at 8:40 AM; Tuesday, March 17 ECG moved to 12:50 PM followed by a Dr. Patel visit at 1:20 PM in Suite 4C. Marcus has said these follow-up times work for him right now and asked that they be kept in the portal. The scheduled Monday nurse callback is now taking place, with nurse Jamison checking how Marcus has been feeling since Friday. Marcus's Tuesday visit is now scheduled after noon; scheduler Terry confirmed Tuesday is ECG at 12:50 PM and visit at 1:20 PM in Suite 4C.
